title: JavaScript enabled in a WebView
description: With JavaScript on, content loaded in the WebView runs scripts. Combined with untrusted content, native bridges or file access, it becomes an XSS and interface-abuse vector.
remediation: Enable it only when needed and only for trusted origins (HTTPS and a host allowlist).
falsePositives: Very common and legitimate in apps that load only their own content. Relevance depends on the loaded URL and the other settings.

title: addJavascriptInterface native bridge
description: Exposes Java methods annotated with @JavascriptInterface to the page's JavaScript. Any content loaded in this WebView (iframes included) can call them.
remediation: Restrict the WebView to trusted origins, minimise the exposed methods and prefer WebMessageListener/addWebMessageListener with an origin allowlist.
falsePositives: Safe in practice when the WebView only loads bundled, trusted content.

title: File access enabled in a WebView
description: Lets the WebView load file:// URLs, which may expose the app's internal files when combined with third-party-controlled URLs.
remediation: Keep it disabled (default false from targetSdk 30) and use WebViewAssetLoader for local content.
falsePositives: Harmless if the WebView never loads external URLs.

title: setAllowFileAccessFromFileURLs(true)
description: Scripts in file:// pages can read other local files.
remediation: Do not enable it; use WebViewAssetLoader.
falsePositives: Rarely needed. Check whether the code is reachable.

title: setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(true)
description: Scripts in file:// pages can access any origin, including reading local files and sending them out.
remediation: Do not enable it; use WebViewAssetLoader.

title: WebView debugging enabled
description: Allows inspecting the content of every WebView in the app through DevTools with the device connected.
remediation: Enable it only in debug builds (for example behind BuildConfig.DEBUG).
falsePositives: It may sit behind a debug check that JADX preserved; check the context.

title: loadUrl with a non-literal argument
description: The URL comes from a variable. If it can come from outside (Intent, deep link, network), the WebView may load third-party-controlled content.
remediation: Validate scheme and host against an allowlist before loading.
falsePositives: Frequent: the URL may be a constant built elsewhere. It is only a lead to follow the data manually.
